answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a small time-locked stake that only matures after a public probation, like a violet sapling planted in a shared grove that must survive one full season before it bears fruit. A gale of fake accounts still costs the attacker one stake per identity, and peers can slash the stake when an identity is caught copying work or double-spending reputation, so spawning thousands of clones becomes expensive instead of free.
